tx-acid.title: Four promises, and who keeps each one
tx-acid.description: The four ACID properties side by side: atomicity undoes partial work, consistency is mostly the application's rules, isolation separates concurrent work, and durability keeps committed data.
tx-acid.note: Only consistency depends mostly on your code; the database keeps the other three.

tx-read-committed.title: Read committed during an open transfer
tx-read-committed.description: T1 writes 150 without committing, T2 still reads the committed 200, T3 waits on T1's row lock, and T1's commit releases both.
tx-read-committed.note: Readers see only committed values, and writers queue on the row lock.

tx-snapshot.title: A snapshot reader ignores later commits
tx-snapshot.description: Transaction 100 takes a snapshot showing 480 seats, transaction 102 commits a newer version, transaction 100 still reads 480, and the old version is removed only when no snapshot needs it.
tx-snapshot.note: Each write adds a version, and the snapshot decides which version a reader sees.

tx-lost-update.title: Two writers read the same balance
tx-lost-update.description: Two payments both read a balance of 100, then write values computed from it, so the second write discards the first debit and the balance ends at 50 instead of 20.
tx-lost-update.note: Should be 20. Atomic updates, row locks, or compare-and-set prevent this.

tx-write-skew.title: Two bookings pass the same capacity check
tx-write-skew.description: Two transactions each count 99 bookings out of 100 places, each inserts its own row, and both commit, leaving 101 bookings with no write conflict to detect.
tx-write-skew.note: Materialize the conflict: a counter row makes the second buyer collide with the first.

tx-serializable.title: Three serializable methods, plus the common shortcut
tx-serializable.description: Serial execution runs one transaction at a time, two-phase locking blocks on conflict, serializable snapshot isolation aborts on risky patterns, and many teams stay at a weaker level with targeted guards.
tx-serializable.note: Whichever you choose, test what your database's level name actually prevents.
